summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of neurogenic bladder from a prior gunshot wound, chronic indwelling Foley catheter, type II diabetes, and right below-knee amputation was admitted for evaluation of two weeks of left-sided flank pain. She was afebrile with no signs of systemic infection. Initial urinalysis showed bacteria, but given her history of chronic urinary colonization with multidrug-resistant organisms and absence of infection markers, antibiotics were discontinued. Imaging of the pelvis and left hip showed no fracture, with findings consistent with degenerative changes and a stable bone island; bursitis was suspected as a pain source. Her anemia was chronic and stable. Pain management was optimized with increased ibuprofen, and she was discharged home with instructions to follow up with primary care for ongoing hip pain management and catheter care.
